uncertainties: Small Rashi script; the first word looks like הס״ן, which I read as הש״ץ

page_completeness_notes: Two columns: the main Modim on the right and Modim deRabbanan on the left, followed by full-width text. The page ends with כָּאָמוּר:

blocks.text: 145 Musaph for the New Year 145
While the Kohanim make their way to the דוכן, the congregation say: ותערב
uncertainties: Italic; the Hebrew words are embedded in the instruction

blocks.text: ותערב

May our entreaty be pleasing to Thee like the whole-offering and the sacrifice. O Merciful One, restore Thy presence to Zion in Thy great mercies and the order of worship to Jerusalem. Let our eyes behold Thy return to Zion in compassion and let us serve Thee there in awe as in olden times and former years.
uncertainties: 'whole-offering' is broken across a line at its real hyphen, so the hyphen stays. 'pres-ence' was a line-wrap hyphen and has been joined

blocks.text: ברוך
Blessed art Thou, O Lord, whom alone we wish to worship in awe.
מודים

We thank Thee for Thou art the Lord our God and the God of our fathers for ever and ever. The Rock of our life, the Shield of our salvation art Thou from generation to generation. We thank Thee and tell of Thy fame for our life that is delivered in Thy hand for our souls that are entrusted to Thee and for Thy miracles that are daily with us and for Thy wonders and benefits at all times, evening, morning and noon. O Thou who art good for Thy mercies never end, O Thou who showest mercy for Thy sindnesses never cease, ever have we trusted in Thee.
uncertainties: The source prints 'sindnesses' (presumably a misprint for 'kindnesses'), and I kept it as printed

blocks.text: Congregation:
uncertainties: Italic label over the right column

blocks.text: מודים

We thank Thee because Thou art the Lord our God and the God of our fathers, the God of all flesh, our Creator, the Creator of the beginning. Blessings and thanks to Thy Great and Holy Name for having kept us alive and let us survive. So mayest Thou further keep us alive and let us survive and gather our exiles to the court-yards of Thy Sanctuary in order to observe Thy statutes and do Thy will and serve Thee whole-heartedly; wherefore we thank Thee. Blessed be God to whom thanks are due.
uncertainties: The line-wrap hyphens in 'Cre-ator', 'may-est' and 'Bless-ed' have been joined. I kept 'court-yards' and 'whole-heartedly' as printed, but whether those hyphens are real or just line wraps is unclear

blocks.text: ועל
For all of them may Thy Name, O our King, be continually blessed and exalted for ever and ever.
וכתוב
And inscribe for a good life all the children of Thy Covenant.
וכל

And all the living thank Thee, Selah, and praise Thy Name in truth, O God of our salvation and of our aid, Selah! Blessed art Thou, O Lord, All-benevolent, whose name is goodness and unto whom it is becoming to give thanks.
אלהינו

Our God and God of our fathers, bless us with the threefold blessing that is written in the Torah through Moses Thy servant and was uttered by the mouth of Aaron and his sons the priests, Thy holy people, as it is said:

page_completeness_notes: The English does not render the הש״ץ מסיים / הש״ץ בקול labels. 'Congregation:' is the only role label on the page.
